# Svalboard — Hands Down Neu + Arensito symbols

Vial keymap for the Svalboard Lightly, ported from my Glove80.

## Load it

1. Open [KeyBard](https://captdeaf.github.io/keybard/) (or the Vial app) with the
   Svalboard plugged in.
2. **Load** → `SvalHandsDownNeu.vil`.

No reflash needed — Vial writes the keymap to the keyboard live.

## Layers

**Layer 0 — Hands Down Neu**

```
w f m p v   / . q " '
r s n t b   , a e i h
x c l d g   ; u o y k
```

`z` and `j` sit on the right pinky's East and West laterals. On the Glove80 they
live in the outer column, which the Svalboard doesn't have.

Note this is my Glove80's Neu, not upstream's: `;` on the right inner column
where [alanreiser.com](https://sites.google.com/alanreiser.com/handsdown/home/hands-down-neu)
publishes `-`.

**Layer 1 — Arensito symbols** (hold `MO(1)`, right thumb)

```
{ } [ ] @   & _ < > $
; / - 0 :   \ 1 ( ) =
6 7 8 9 +   * 2 3 4 5
```

Backtick is on `MO(1)` + left pinky **West** (so `~` is that plus shift). Arensito's
`{` takes the slot where Svalboard's stock config kept the only `KC_GRAVE`, and
the Glove80 has grave on its base layer — losing it would be a regression, so
it gets reseated on a lateral Arensito leaves free.

**Layer 2** — nav and F-keys, untouched from Svalboard's stock config.

**Spare laterals on layer 0** are inherited from the stock Colemak-DHm config,
not ported: openers on the left hand's outward laterals, closers on the right's,
plus `-` and Delete on the left pinky.

```
L index/middle/ring West = ( { [        R index/middle/ring East = ) } ]
L pinky East = -                        L pinky West = Delete
```

These are columns the Svalboard doesn't have and the Glove80 fills from its
outer column, so there was nothing to port onto them. Keeping Svalboard's
assignment is a decision, not an accident — `build.py` lists them in
`SPARE_LATERALS`.

Thumb clusters are also stock:

```
L: ctrl tab shift bspc esc gui
R: alt enter MO(1) space MO(2) gui
```

## Host setup

Nothing to do. Hyprland scopes my Colemak variant to the two internal keyboards
by device name (`hyprland.nix`), so the Svalboard falls through to the default
plain `us` — which is what a firmware-side layout wants. Adding the Svalboard to
that `device` list would double-translate every keystroke.

## Regenerating

```sh
python3 build.py
```

`build.py` rewrites the 40 finger-cup positions on layers 0 and 1 of
`SvalCOLEMAKDHM.vil` (vendored from
[svalboard/svalboard-configs](https://github.com/svalboard/svalboard-configs)),
leaving thumbs, layer 2, and Vial metadata alone.

The interesting part is the geometry. Svalboard `.vil` layers are 10×6:

```
row 0 = left thumb        row 5 = right thumb
rows 1-4 = left  index, middle, ring, pinky
rows 6-9 = right index, middle, ring, pinky
cols     = [South, East, Center, North, West, unused]
```

Each finger has only N/C/S for its column, so the layout's inner-index column
spills onto one inward lateral per finger — `inner-top → middle`,
`inner-home → index`, `inner-bottom → ring`. That convention is Svalboard's own,
reverse-engineered from their Colemak-DHm config.

Since that mapping is a guess about matrix order that would fail *silently* —
producing a scrambled but valid-looking keymap — `build.py` refuses to emit
anything until it has run the stock Colemak-DHm block back through the same code
path and reproduced all 30 alpha positions in the shipped `.vil` exactly.

directly into chat, or export it: Advanced Settings → Enable local config → back
to Edit → Download.

1. **Backtick and tilde were untypable.** Confirmed it myself before fixing: Arensito's `{` lands on the one slot holding the stock config's only `KC_GRAVE`, and nothing in 16 layers supplied it. Your Glove80 has grave on its base layer, so this was a regression against the source, not a choice. Reseated on `MO(1)` + left pinky **West**.
2. **Added `check_no_orphans()`** — fails the build if any keycode vanishes from every layer with no shift- or ISO-reachable substitute. I removed the fix and watched it fail on `KC_GRAVE` before trusting it green. The other 8 dropped keycodes are all `!#%^` (shift+digit, layer 1 has all ten digits) or ISO-only.
3. **The 8 layer-0 spare laterals** were inherited from Colemak by accident. Now recorded in `SPARE_LATERALS` and in the README: `( { [` on left outward laterals, `) } ]` on right, `-`/Delete on left pinky.
4. **Docstring cited `glove80-hdneu.json`**, which was never in the repo. Now cites the layout UUID.
5. **Deferred — `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`.** The reviewer flagged that `.claude/settings.json` still wires seven `entire` hooks. That deletion was already unstaged in your tree when I started and isn't mine, so I left it alone — flagging rather than reverting, per your parallel-session rule.
```
self-test OK: 30 Colemak-DHm positions reproduced from place()
orphan check OK: 8 keycodes dropped, all shift- or ISO-explained
wrote SvalHandsDownNeu.vil: 32 base + 31 symbol positions, 16 layers
idempotent: rebuild is byte-identical
all 26 letters on layer 0: YES
```

```
LAYER 0                      LAYER 1

  r s n t b   , a e i h        ; / - 0 :   \ 1 ( ) =
  x c l d g   ; u o y k        6 7 8 9 +   * 2 3 4 5
```

Root cause found — and it means installing Vial alone would *not* have fixed it.

**The Svalboard's hidraw nodes are root-only:**
```
hidraw12-15 = Svalboard lightly (303A:4044)
```

No Vial/QMK udev rule exists on this box. Browser KeyBard uses WebHID → `/dev/hidraw` → permission denied, silently. Same wall Vial would hit.

So it's two things: a udev rule (needs root) **and** the app.

=== system/deploy ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Run as your normal user (e.g. `mise run deploy`), NOT under sudo: the sops
# steps below decrypt with your GCP key under $HOME and each privileged install
# sudo's itself. Running the whole script as root points $HOME at /root, so sops
# can't find the key (and root has no KMS creds) -- fail fast instead.
if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "system/deploy: run as your user (try 'mise run system:deploy'), not root." >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$(dirname "$0")"
find etc/ -type d | while read -r d; do sudo mkdir -p "/${d}"; done
find etc/ -type f | while read -r f; do sudo cp -v "${f}" "/${f}"; done

# polkit only scans /usr/share/polkit-1/actions for action definitions, which
# etc/ can't reach; install Bitwarden's unlock action there so its "system
# authentication" biometric prompt is authorized on this non-NixOS host.
sudo install -Dvm644 polkit-1/actions/com.bitwarden.Bitwarden.policy \
  /usr/share/polkit-1/actions/com.bitwarden.Bitwarden.policy

# ── gnome-keyring: let the home-manager unit own the daemon ───────────────────
# The login collection can only be unlocked at daemon startup, so home-manager
# runs its own gnome-keyring.service whose ExecStart unseals the passphrase from
# the TPM (see gnome-keyring-tpm in home.nix). Mask Arch's packaged units so a
# second, *locked* daemon can't be started behind our back -- its socket unit
# listens on %t/keyring/control and would socket-activate one on any control-op.
# This is only half the job: the D-Bus activation files in /usr/share also start
# a locked daemon, and systemd masking does nothing about those. They are
# shadowed from ~/.local/share/dbus-1/services by home.nix.
sudo rm -f /etc/systemd/user/sockets.target.wants/gnome-keyring-daemon.socket
sudo ln -sfn /dev/null /etc/systemd/user/gnome-keyring-daemon.socket
sudo ln -sfn /dev/null /etc/systemd/user/gnome-keyring-daemon.service

# Unsealing the gnome-keyring passphrase reads /dev/tpmrm0, which is root:tss 0660.
# Takes effect at next login, not in the current session.
if ! id -nG "$USER" | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -qx tss; then
  sudo gpasswd -a "$USER" tss
fi

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
# systemd-oomd parses oomd.conf (and its drop-ins) once at startup, so a changed
# etc/systemd/oomd.conf.d/* must be followed by an actual restart. `enable --now`
# is NOT enough: --now only *starts* a stopped unit, so on a host where oomd is
# already running it is a silent no-op and the new limits sit on disk unapplied.
# `restart` covers both cases (starts it if stopped) and kills nothing on its way
# through -- oomd holds no state worth preserving across a reload.
sudo systemctl enable systemd-oomd
sudo systemctl restart systemd-oomd

# `drovr serve` binds 0.0.0.0 on this host and has NO authentication, so the
# allowlist in etc/nftables.d/drovr.nft is the only thing between the pod network
# and every run's contents. `restart` rather than `enable --now`, for the same
# reason as oomd above: --now is a no-op on an already-active unit, which would
# leave an edited ruleset sitting on disk unapplied.
#
# NOTE the unit loads its own `inet drovr` table and nothing else. Do NOT enable
# nftables.service to persist this instead: Arch ships /etc/nftables.conf as a

content.text: Making the changes. Rule matches the vial magic serial, so it covers every Vial board rather than hardcoding Svalboard's VID.

input.content:
# Vial-compatible keyboards (Svalboard Lightly and friends).
#
# The config interface is a /dev/hidraw* node, which udev creates 0600 root:root
# by default. Without this rule Vial and browser-based KeyBard both enumerate the
# keyboard and then fail to open it -- the failure surfaces as "no keyboard
# detected", with nothing pointing at permissions.
#
# Matching the vial magic serial rather than VID/PID covers every Vial board on
# one rule, which is what upstream's own rule does. Verified against this host:
#   /sys/bus/usb/devices/9-1.4.1.2/serial = vial:f64c2b3c
#
# TAG+="uaccess" is the mechanism that normally does the work -- logind puts an
# ACL on the node for whoever owns the active seat. GROUP is the fallback for
# sessions logind doesn't treat as seated, which is a live concern on this host
# (systemd-homed user, uid 60006, absent from /etc/passwd -- see home.nix). Note
# upstream's rule says GROUP="users", which would be a no-op here: sauyon is in
# input, video, audio, wheel, realtime, docker and tss, but not users.
KERNEL=="hidraw*", SUBSYSTEM=="hidraw", ATTRS{serial}=="*vial:f64c2b3c*", MODE="0660", GROUP="input", TAG+="uaccess", TAG+="udev-acl"

Fixed and verified. One thing needs your call.

**It works now — try it: run `Vial`** (capitalized — that's the binary name).

**The actual problem was never the software.** Your Svalboard's `/dev/hidraw*` nodes were `0600 root:root`. Browser KeyBard enumerated the keyboard via WebHID, then couldn't open it, and reported nothing useful. Installing an editor alone would have hit the identical wall.

Two things landed:

1. **`system/etc/udev/rules.d/92-vial.rules`** — installed to `/etc/` and reloaded. Matches the vial magic serial (`vial:f64c2b3c`) rather than VID/PID, so it covers any Vial board.
2. **`pkgs.vial`** in `home.nix` — `home-manager switch --flake .#utsuho` applied clean.

I ran only the narrow install, not `mise run system:deploy` — that script also restarts oomd and nftables and masks keyring units, which you didn't ask for.

**Worth knowing:** upstream's rule uses `GROUP="users"`, which would be a no-op — you're not in `users`. And I verified `TAG+="uaccess"` produced **no ACL** on this host (`getfacl` shows no `user:sauyon` entry), consistent with the systemd-homed seat issue already documented in `home.nix`. So `GROUP="input"` is doing the real work, not redundancy.

**Evidence, end to end:**
```
hidraw12-15  crw-rw---- root input     (was crw------- root root)
open O_RDWR as sauyon .............. OK on all four
Vial raw HID (usage page 0xFF60) ... hidraw13
VIA protocol version ............... 9
Vial protocol / uid ................ 6 / 0x4829f621f27d181b
```
That uid matches the `uid` field in both `.vil` files — so the keymap I generated is for this exact board.

---

**Your call: the push is blocked, and it isn't my conflict.**

`master` diverged. A parallel session made 5 commits on the remote (drovr pin bumps, deleting `system/etc/nftables.d/drovr.nft` and `drovr-firewall.service`, trimming `system/deploy`). Local has 3 commits of mine plus 2 that aren't mine.

Dry-run merge says:

```
flake.lock CONFLICT
```

The `flake.lock` conflict is between that session's local commits and the remote — **none of my commits touch `flake.lock`**. Resolving it means picking which drovr pin wins, and per your parallel-session rule I'm not guessing at that.


Tell me which drovr pin you want and I'll rebase and push, or take it yourself with `git pull --rebase origin master`.

Two smaller things still open: `/code-review` hasn't seen the udev rule or the `home.nix` change; and the unstaged `D .opencode/plugins/entire.ts` is still untouched.

The fix that would work from here is `xhost +local:`, which disables X access control for every local process for the rest of your session. That's a security change to your running desktop and it's your call, not mine — so I stopped.

**KeyBard is open in Chromium now.** Click Connect, then load `~/devel/dotfiles/keyboards/svalboard/SvalHandsDownNeu.vil`.

```
class=chromium   title=KeyBard interface - Chromium
```

**Vial can't run on this box right now, and it's not Vial's fault.** `xdpyinfo` — a plain X client with no bubblewrap — fails identically:

```
Authorization required, but no authorization protocol specified
unable to open display ":0"
```

Your Hyprland session started **Aug 17** and its Xwayland came up with no auth file:
```
Xwayland :0 -rootless -core -listenfd 57 -listenfd 58 -displayfd 128 -wm 125
                    ↑ no -auth
```
`XAUTHORITY` is unset in Hyprland's own environment and no cookie file exists anywhere. Xwayland reads its auth file only at startup, so this is unfixable on a running server — **every X11 app on this machine is broken until the compositor restarts**, not just Vial. Chromium is Wayland-native, which is why it sidesteps it.

Also worth knowing: the running compositor is **0.56.0**, the installed binary is **0.56.2**. The session is a version behind.

**I am not going to suggest you just log out.** Your own notes document that a passwordless login before the homed LUKS home unlocks starts `systemd --user` with `HOME=/`, which makes every home-manager user unit invisible for the whole boot — no waybar, no kanshi — and breaks `home-manager switch` at `Activating sops-nix`. A relogin is exactly the operation that triggers it, and the tailscaled patch that fixes it is built but **not deployed**. That's your call to make with eyes open, not a throwaway suggestion from me.

Three options, in the order I'd take them:

1. **Use KeyBard in Chromium** — open now, no restart, no risk. Does everything Vial does.
2. **Run Vial nested** — `cage 0.3.1` and `xwayland-satellite 0.8.2` are both in nixpkgs and would give Vial its own working Xwayland without touching your session. Say the word and I'll wire one up.
3. **Restart the session** — fixes X11 generally and picks up 0.56.2, but carries the homed risk above. Worth doing deliberately, ideally after deploying that tailscaled patch.

The udev fix is doing its job either way — that's what unblocked KeyBard, which failed for you originally purely on permissions.

# Svalboard — Hands Down Neu + Arensito symbols

Vial keymap for the Svalboard Lightly, ported from my Glove80.

## Load it

1. Open [KeyBard](https://captdeaf.github.io/keybard/) (or the Vial app) with the
   Svalboard plugged in.
2. **Load** → `SvalHandsDownNeu.vil`.

No reflash needed — Vial writes the keymap to the keyboard live.

## Layers

**Layer 0 — Hands Down Neu**

```
w f m p v   / . q " '
r s n t b   , a e i h
x c l d g   ; u o y k
```

`z` and `j` sit on the right pinky's East and West laterals. On the Glove80 they
live in the outer column, which the Svalboard doesn't have.

Note this is my Glove80's Neu, not upstream's: `;` on the right inner column
where [alanreiser.com](https://sites.google.com/alanreiser.com/handsdown/home/hands-down-neu)
publishes `-`.

**Layer 1 — Arensito symbols** (hold `MO(1)`, right thumb)

```
{ } [ ] @   & _ < > $
; / - 0 :   \ 1 ( ) =
6 7 8 9 +   * 2 3 4 5
```

Backtick is on `MO(1)` + left pinky **West** (so `~` is that plus shift). Arensito's
`{` takes the slot where Svalboard's stock config kept the only `KC_GRAVE`, and
the Glove80 has grave on its base layer — losing it would be a regression, so
it gets reseated on a lateral Arensito leaves free.

**Layer 2** — nav and F-keys, untouched from Svalboard's stock config.

**Spare laterals on layer 0** are inherited from the stock Colemak-DHm config,
not ported: openers on the left hand's outward laterals, closers on the right's,
plus `-` and Delete on the left pinky.

```
L index/middle/ring West = ( { [        R index/middle/ring East = ) } ]
L pinky East = -                        L pinky West = Delete
```

These are columns the Svalboard doesn't have and the Glove80 fills from its
outer column, so there was nothing to port onto them. Keeping Svalboard's
assignment is a decision, not an accident — `build.py` lists them in
`SPARE_LATERALS`.

Thumb clusters are also stock:

```
L: ctrl tab shift bspc esc gui
R: alt enter MO(1) space MO(2) gui
```

## Host setup

Nothing to do. Hyprland scopes my Colemak variant to the two internal keyboards
by device name (`hyprland.nix`), so the Svalboard falls through to the default
plain `us` — which is what a firmware-side layout wants. Adding the Svalboard to
that `device` list would double-translate every keystroke.

## Regenerating

```sh
python3 build.py
```

`build.py` rewrites the 40 finger-cup positions on layers 0 and 1 of
`SvalCOLEMAKDHM.vil` (vendored from
[svalboard/svalboard-configs](https://github.com/svalboard/svalboard-configs)),
leaving thumbs, layer 2, and Vial metadata alone.

The interesting part is the geometry. Svalboard `.vil` layers are 10×6:

```
row 0 = left thumb        row 5 = right thumb
rows 1-4 = left  index, middle, ring, pinky
rows 6-9 = right index, middle, ring, pinky
cols     = [South, East, Center, North, West, unused]
```

Each finger has only N/C/S for its column, so the layout's inner-index column
spills onto one inward lateral per finger — `inner-top → middle`,
`inner-home → index`, `inner-bottom → ring`. That convention is Svalboard's own,
reverse-engineered from their Colemak-DHm config.

Since that mapping is a guess about matrix order that would fail *silently* —
producing a scrambled but valid-looking keymap — `build.py` refuses to emit
anything until it has run the stock Colemak-DHm block back through the same code
path and reproduced all 30 alpha positions in the shipped `.vil` exactly.

A second guard catches the other silent failure: writing 60 positions over a
config we didn't author drops whatever was underneath. `check_no_orphans()`
fails the build if any keycode disappears from all 16 layers with no shift- or
ISO-explained substitute. That is how `` ` `` and `~` were caught.

2026-01-20"), layer `Base` and layer `symbols`.
